code_verdict: APPROVED, code only. This does not cover data integration. I read all seven bundle files (realizations.py, baseline.py, build.py and the four test modules) along with the v4 review, the collected test list, the v6 log and the audit. The medium v4 gap is fixed. (1) attesting_controls now walks the segments returned first by prepare_documents(unit, readings). A unit-level canonical_whole occurrence therefore appears as one canonical=target segment, and its unit conditions, marked, instructions, head and opening_page are bound through the raw unit. The collapse loses no segment scope: prepare_unit only collapses when every source segment is within PLAIN_SEGMENT_KEYS, so no segment can carry conditions or condition_end_corresp. In every other case the effective list keeps the raw length and order, so the segment indexes and endpoint lookups still match the raw data. canonical_home attesters are skipped as the owner when they point at their own home, which is correct. (2) Both sides are now symmetric. The covered set is {target} plus the identities of the resolved range segments, and review_payloads now passes selected_ids = {target} plus the selected segment identities. Explicit whole-target pointers and canonical_whole callers therefore see each other. A caller of a nested Bible segment inside a whole-text host and a caller of the whole text also bind both ways, through the range segment identities. None is excluded on the caller side. (3) The tests cover the mutual staleness of unit conditions between explicit=text_corresp and canonical_whole in both directions, and a non-pure ranged attester whose canonical_end binds a single-part caller, checked both directly through attesting_controls and through the payload. The condition-error test now expects one exact message per case ('typed feature structures' twice, 'requires conditions' once). All three cases get past the CANONICAL_OCCURRENCE_KEYS gate, so they really do reach validate_occurrence_controls. (4) Evidence: the collected list gives 42 + 8 + 15 + 93 = 158 tests across the four modules, matching '158 passed, 146 subtests passed' in importer-tests-v6.log. As you directed, I accept as intentional that the redirection preflight allows PLAIN mapping fields, on the condition that the host-transfer evidence is required as a data gate. I also leave the broad DRAFT-label check in build.py out of scope, since it errs toward caution. One scope note, not blocking: canonical_corrections.py and opensiddur.exporter.urn.split_range are still not in the bundle. They are covered only through tests, and this approval does not certify their source. The v6 log also does not record the pytest command.
